notes.n6.frontier: An oligopoly of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, with xAI (now within SpaceX), Meta, Microsoft and Amazon; well-funded new labs (Thinking Machines, SSI) have not yet shipped frontier-scale public models.
notes.n6.open: Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot, Zhipu, MiniMax) lead open-weight downloads and benchmarks; US response includes Reflection AI, gpt-oss, Nemotron and Ai2; Zhipu and MiniMax listed in Hong Kong in Jan 2026.
notes.n6.enterprise: Consolidating: Cohere and Aleph Alpha agreed to merge (2026) to build a transatlantic sovereign enterprise vendor; others (AI21, Writer) bundle models with agent platforms.
notes.n6.small: Driven by on-device and cost: big labs' small lines (Gemma, Phi, Qwen, Apple) compete with efficiency specialists (Liquid AI, Zyphra, Multiverse).
notes.n6.image: Crowded and global: US (Midjourney, Runway, Luma), Germany (Black Forest Labs) and China (Kling, Hailuo, Seedance, Vidu, Wan) compete; licensing settlements and studio deals are now differentiators.
notes.n6.audio: ElevenLabs leads voice; STT is contested by Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Speechmatics and big-lab models; music generation moved from litigation to label settlements (Suno-WMG, Udio-UMG, 2025).
notes.n6.code: Frontier general models dominate coding; tool makers (Cursor, Cognition) now train their own models, and open coders (Qwen-Coder, Kimi, Devstral) compete on cost.
notes.n6.science: Mix of Alphabet/NVIDIA/Microsoft platforms and heavily funded startups; 2025-26 trend is 'AI scientist' labs pairing models with autonomous wet labs (Periodic, Lila).
notes.n6.world: Pre-commercial but heavily funded: robotics foundation models (Physical Intelligence, Skild) and world models (World Labs, AMI Labs $1.03B seed Mar 2026, Genie, Cosmos).
notes.n6.sovereign: India's IndiaAI Mission funds 12 builders; BharatGen gets Rs 1,058.52 crore, 4x the next (Medianama, Apr 2026).
notes.n6.embed: Consolidated into data platforms: Voyage to MongoDB and Jina to Elastic (2025); Cohere, OpenAI, Google and open Qwen/BGE models dominate.
notes.n6.train: Open-source frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, Megatron, TRL, verl) are the base; fine-tuning-as-a-service is being absorbed by clouds (OpenPipe to CoreWeave, Predibase to Rubrik) while Thinking Machines' Tinker targets RL fine-tuning.
notes.n6.opt: Compression startups are being acquired by chip/platform owners (Neural Magic to Red Hat, Deci to NVIDIA, Edge Impulse to Qualcomm); independent players are Multiverse, Pruna, Nota, Embedl.
notes.n6.safety: Split between government institutes (UK AISI, US CAISI), non-profit evaluators (METR, Apollo) and commercial red-teaming/interpretability; enterprise AI-security startups mostly acquired by cybersecurity firms in 2025.
notes.n6.hub: Hugging Face is the default open hub (ModelScope in China); cloud catalogues (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex) and routers (OpenRouter) are the commercial distribution channels.
notes.n6.domain: Splits into frontier-lab health releases (MedGemma) and specialist labs in bio, health and legal; most value sits in biology models with proprietary data.
notes.n6.weights: No standalone market yet: indemnity is bundled by model vendors, weight security by model-security and confidential-computing vendors, licensing norms by Hugging Face and OSI.
